claims.statement: Bosch estimates maintenance of most heat-pump systems at about 1,000 PLN annually and frames regular service as a way to prevent higher repair costs, establishing a visible paid maintenance event.
Homeowners already bear maintenance and repair spend on a high-value heating asset; willingness to prepay a multi-brand independent plan is not established.
A plausible control path is a funded seasonal capacity-reservation contract with qualified technicians and a direct annual homeowner plan; neither side is contracted.

Bosch describes more than 500 authorized service technicians nationally and ties additional warranty years for selected heat pumps to paid inspections by authorized partners, confirming organized service labor and warranty-driven visits.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Property owner or household member responsible for heating
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Multi-brand portability, local response transparency, and continuity when the original installer is unavailable must justify the plan
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The homeowner may already have an installer or manufacturer relationship; the proposed plan relationship does not exist
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Installer handoff, service-partner referral, local search, or property-manager portfolio

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Installer or property-manager referral share and local-search spend
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual prepayment can fund reserved capacity before visits, subject to refund and claim reserves
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Depends on negotiated visit cost, geographic density, callout incidence, and exclusions; currently unknown
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Scheduling, homeowner support, service documentation, repeat-visit handling, and vendor coordination
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Insurance, service terms, consumer rights, contractor checks, data security, and quality audits
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Target 1,200-1,800 PLN annual homeowner plan with defined included maintenance and discounted callouts
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Technician visit, travel, remote triage, payment fees, basic consumables, and plan claims

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Manufacturers, authorized networks, installers, utilities, and insurers can bundle maintenance and extended warranty
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Annual plan activation and completed maintenance are paid; measurable loss is emergency downtime, repeat visits, warranty loss, and excess energy associated with poor operation
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Approaching annual or warranty inspection, first fault, installer unavailability, or winter reliability concern
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual pre-season service and capacity reservation

contrary_evidence: Bosch already operates a large authorized network and manufacturer warranty program, demonstrating strong incumbent control.
Not every heat pump legally requires annual maintenance, reducing urgency outside warranty terms.
Manufacturer authorization can be brand-specific, limiting genuinely multi-brand fulfillment.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive seasonal capacity-reservation agreement with prepaid minimum volume; none secured
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Operate planned maintenance only through multiple replaceable pay-per-job providers and exclude guaranteed response times
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The homeowner may already have an installer or manufacturer relationship; the proposed plan relationship does not exist
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed one heating season or 12 months; not agreed
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The family renewable-energy installation firm can lawfully support bounded workflow discovery and potential opt-in referrals, but no technician capacity or customer contract is secured
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Each service business controlling its technician calendar
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed annual renewal before the heating season
critical_control_point.subject: Qualified technician maintenance and response slots

economics.acquisition_route: Installer referrals, property managers, local search, and service-partner cross-sell
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Conditional path: 5,000 plans at 1,450 PLN average equals 7.25m PLN recurring billings; a dense profitable service network could exceed 5m PLN in value, but capacity terms and loss ratios are unknown
economics.founder_time: One geography, limited brands, and outsourced field labor can fit 3-5 hours daily; guaranteed emergency coverage cannot until operations mature
economics.gross_margin_basis: Annual fee less technician capacity and visits, travel, support, claims, channel share, and reserve costs
economics.payback: Customer value is reliability and documented maintenance; financial payback is uncertain and should not be overstated
economics.pricing: Discovery hypothesis: 1,200-1,800 PLN annual plan with one defined inspection and bounded response benefits
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual renewal tied to maintenance and heating-season confidence

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Multi-brand fault, parts, travel-time, seasonality, and first-visit-resolution data improve capacity placement and triage
fingerprint.customer: Polish homeowners and small property managers operating residential heat pumps outside dense metropolitan service coverage
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer handoff after commissioning, property-manager portfolios, insurer referrals, and targeted local search
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Annual maintenance coordination and response plan funded by homeowner subscription and fulfilled through reserved technician capacity
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Property owner pays an annual plan when a defined maintenance visit and response entitlement are reserved
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Annual maintenance, warranty deadline, efficiency drift, fault alert, or loss of heat during peak season

founder_fit: The family firm supplies a lawful, bounded route to observe installation-to-aftercare handoffs
Scheduling, triage, failure prediction, and capacity planning fit data-science skills
Operational outcomes such as response time and first-visit resolution are measurable
Partner technicians perform physical work, allowing the founder to focus on an automatable operating system
risks: Missed winter service levels can create property damage and reputational loss
Technician scarcity can eliminate margin exactly when customers need service
Consumer plan wording can resemble an insurance promise if drafted poorly
Manufacturers or original installers can block access or bundle equivalent coverage

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: annual homeowner aftercare plan with managed field fulfillment
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: pre reserved qualified technician slots by geography and season
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: reliable qualified service firms honoring prices documentation and response windows

structure.commercial_archetype: Managed aftercare plan backed by technician capacity reservations
structure.control_point: Contracted service slots during seasonal demand peaks
structure.critical_dependency: Qualified, geographically dense service technicians willing to reserve capacity and honor service levels

thesis: Observed purchasing and labor-allocation signal: Bosch publicly estimates typical heat-pump maintenance near 1,000 PLN annually, runs a national authorized-service network, and conditions extended warranty on paid technical inspections. Sell homeowners a multi-brand annual plan backed by pre-reserved qualified technician slots, documented maintenance, remote symptom intake, and bounded winter-response service rather than an unbacked lead-generation directory.
title: Heat-Pump Service Capacity Reserve
uncertainties: Regional technician capacity, reservation price, and winter response reliability
Installed-base density by brand around initial launch geography
Callout frequency and exclusions needed for sustainable plan economics
Whether third-party coordination preserves manufacturer warranty
